rationale: The protocol goes live for every shift at once, so the evaluation is an implementation study: RE-AIM organises reach, adoption, implementation fidelity and maintenance, and an interrupted time series of weekly service measures, with season and demand as covariates, estimates the change in waits. Both recorded searches were empty, so the design rests on the investigator's local facts and approvals rather than on retrieved evidence. Reporting follows StaRI.
alternatives: Stepped introduction of the protocol by shift with a comparison (refused: the board has approved go-live for all shifts at once)
Simple before-after comparison of two months (refused: cannot separate the protocol from season and demand)
Satisfaction questionnaire for texters (refused: contacting anonymous texters adds burden at a moment of crisis)
whyNotMoreComplex: A controlled design is ruled out by a service-wide go-live; an interrupted time series with fidelity measures is the strongest design the situation allows and uses data the line already produces.

decision.statement: Evaluate the triage and queue protocol from its go-live on 11 January 2027 as an implementation study, with RE-AIM delivery and acceptance outcomes and an interrupted time series of evening time to first human reply and abandoned conversations, starting the analysis only when message-level timestamps are available under a signed data-sharing agreement.
decision.question: How should the crisis text line's new triage and queue protocol be evaluated?

criteria.text: The protocol goes live for all shifts at once, so delivery, acceptance and service outcomes can only be studied as implemented.
Demand in the first 26 weeks after go-live exceeds the pre-implementation range by more than a third, making the time series uninterpretable.

gates.requirement: Signed data-sharing agreement with the platform vendor giving message-level timestamps and queue data without message content
Research ethics approval of the evaluation
gates.evidence: Approval REB-PSY-2026-071 dated 2026-09-09, conditional on the data-sharing agreement, supplied by the investigator

alternatives: Simple before-after comparison of two months
Monitoring of monthly platform summaries only
decision.note: No ledger claim exists because both recorded searches returned nothing; the decision rests on the confirmed empty searches and the investigator's local facts. The data-sharing gate stays unknown until the agreement is signed.

summary: Implementation study with an interrupted time series recommended; the decision is blocked by one unknown data gate.
